absent: Physical placement and sizing of per processor chunks beyond address window checks.
Concurrency rules for global memory counters and sysinfo readers.
Full struct layouts for zone, node, sysinfo, shrinker info and allocation info.
Contracts and return conventions of count and scan callbacks.
Cache selection, large allocation, sanitizer and trace behaviour beyond dispatch.
Memory group iteration, online checks and identifier lookup semantics.
Debug filesystem helper error behaviour and permission handling.
Numeric values of reserves, watermarks, page size and order limits.

findings.text: Provides query reporting whether numeric address lies inside static per processor area of any possible processor, with optional output canonicalized to boot processor copy; single processor builds always report negative.

Provides translation from per processor pointer to physical address by first testing membership in initial chunk window and per unit windows, then using direct mapping translation for linear addresses and page plus offset composition otherwise.

First chunk allocator choice defaults to automatic and can be set at boot to embed or page where build supports it; empty input is rejected and unrecognized names only warn while retaining prior choice.

Early initialization has two build variants: one reserves module plus dynamic space through embedded first chunk and derives per processor offsets from base displacement plus unit displacements, the other allocates single aligned unit from low memory and configures uniform sizing for solitary group before establishing first chunk; both abort on allocation failure.
Populated page total derives from racy read of populated counter scaled by unit count; asynchronous population remains disabled until late init hook enables it.
Fourth, third, second and first level table footprint constants each equal one page.
Build flags record availability of embedded and paged first chunk construction paths.
Global accounting holds total RAM page count in atomic long plus separate reserve and contiguous reserve counters, all marked read mostly.

Available memory estimate starts from free pages minus reserves, then adds discounted file cache and discounted reclaimable slab plus miscellaneous reclaimable, each reduced by smaller of half value and summed low watermarks, finally clamped at zero.

System information fillers report total, shared, free, buffer and high memory totals with page size as unit; global variant uses system wide counters while node variant aggregates managed and free counts across zone types of given node.

Single global mutex serializes shrinker list mutation, identifier allocation and removal, info expansion across memory groups, debug entry creation detachment and rename, registration and teardown, plus late debug initialization sweep.

Identifier space grows in fixed bit multiples; per node info objects are reallocated on owning node, prior unit contents copied, new backing prepared, published through RCU and old object retired through RCU; offline groups are skipped, already sufficient maps are left alone, and global maximum advances only when every group succeeds.

Lifecycle moves from allocated with default search bias to registered and reference enabled, then through reference drain and completion wait to list removal and RCU deferred destruction; allocation can downgrade memory group awareness when unsupported, registration rejects non allocated objects, and teardown tolerates null and unregistered inputs.

Shrinker control carries flags, search bias, numeric identifier, deferred counters, list linkage, name, debug directory plus numeric debug identifier, count and scan callbacks, reference count, completion, and RCU head.
Deferred counters live per group for aware shrinkers and otherwise in privately allocated array sized singly or per node depending on NUMA awareness.

Debug directory creation is deferred until root exists, uses name plus numeric suffix, exposes count node only when count callback exists and scan node only when scan callback exists; detach clears stored entry under lock and returns prior values for outside lock removal, while rename swaps names atomically and restores old name if underlying rename fails.

Count view queries node zero alone unless NUMA awareness is set, treats empty sentinel as zero, and prints group identifier with per node values only for nonzero totals, stopping early for unaware shrinkers or on pending signal; scan control accepts textual triple of group identifier node and quantity, validates node bounds, ignores zero quantity, resolves and checks online status for aware groups while requiring zero identifier otherwise, then invokes scan callback with matching control.
Reclaim batch size constant equals one hundred twenty eight.

Page allocation shuffling is gated by disabled by default static key plus boolean boot parameter whose setter enables key when true and rejects malformed input; retry limit and maximum shuffle order are fixed.
Shuffle retry count is ten and shuffle order tracks maximum page order.
Allocation flag values are default zero, no lock one, new slab two, no recurse four, no object extension eight; free flag values are default zero and no lock one.
Free flags convert to allocation flags by preserving only no lock intent, and spinning is permitted exactly when no lock is absent.

Sized allocation entry builds context capturing caller size and flags, then chooses sleeping path when spinning allowed and no lock path otherwise; oversize requests go to large allocator with tracing, zero size yields dedicated zero pointer, cacheable sizes select size appropriate cache before allocation, sanitizer adjustment and tracing complete all cacheable paths.

Early per processor failures abort boot, identifier expansion failures roll back identifier allocation, shrinker registration without prior allocation only warns and returns, teardown waits for outstanding lookups before list removal and defers memory release until RCU grace, and debug removal occurs outside global mutex.

Shrinker list uses RCU for traversal with locked mutation and deferred unlink, while per group info pointers are published and retired through RCU and final shrinker memory is freed through RCU callback.
